newsitem.title: USA: Newark ex-police chief jailed for fraud.
newsitem.headline: Newark ex-police chief jailed for fraud.

text.p: The former police chief of Newark was sentenced to 2-1/2 years in prison Monday on charges that are part of a lengthy federal probe into allegations of corruption in New Jersey's largest city.
William Celester, 53, admitted in July that he defrauded the city of $30,000 in police money, accepted more than $26,000 in illegal gratuities and filed a false tax return.
Prosecutors said he gave the money to his wife and girlfriends, made political contributions to Newark Mayor Sharpe James and city council members and paid for vacations to Bermuda and Mexico.
Celester, who had been head of the 1,200-member police department since 1991, was indicted in June on 37 counts and dismissed from his job as police director.

U.S. Attorney Faith Hochberg said, "this sentence has sent a message that we will not tolerate wrongdoing by public officials." The 30-month sentence imposed by Federal Judge Garrett Brown in Trenton was tougher than had been expected under federal guidelines for the fraud charges.
"The public must have faith in the justice system and know that any public official who engages in the corruption of his office will be dealt with most severely," Hochberg said.

The investigation of Celester was part of a continuing federal probe of Newark officials, including James. No charges have been filed against James, who has been mayor since 1986, but his chief of staff, Jackie Mattison, has been indicted and is awaiting trial on charges of taking more than $17,000 in bribes for influencing lucrative city and school board contracts.
